subject: Clarify invoice hold: cross-entity tax nexus and pro-rata billing
messages:
From: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@atlasretail.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: billing@atlasretail.com
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Invoice hold: Aug charges and tax nexus question

Hi Vivek,

We placed a temporary hold on payment for invoice INV-20250801 after our tax team found a potential cross-entity tax nexus issue. The total charged for August looks correct at first glance, but the breakdown shows a ~22% allocation to a UK entity that shouldn't have EU VAT exposure in our org structure.

Can you help explain how Redwood apportions usage across entities when customers have multiple legal entities and shared API keys? We requested usage sample logs but our procurement team flagged that the invoice is live and we'd like a short explanation to give finance while they continue the hold.

Attached: entity-tax-declaration.pdf (we've included our internal tax memo)

Thanks,
Alejandra Ruiz
Head of Finance Operations
Atlas Retail
Attachment: entity-tax-declaration.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@atlasretail.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 11:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Invoice hold: Aug charges and tax nexus question

Alejandra — thanks for the note and the memo. I understand the urgency on your side. Short answer: usage attribution is primarily driven by (1) API key / tenant metadata, (2) the route/model used (hosted vs. dedicated), and (3) any billing-entity override tags you have set in the account. We do not automatically split a single API key across legal entities without an explicit mapping.

What likely happened in your case is one of two things: either a traffic stream was tagged to the UK entity during a staging migration, or a preexisting mapping applied at the org-level caused a subset of sessions to be billed to the UK entity.

Immediate next steps I can take today:
- Share a minimal sample of the per-request attribution (timestamps, request_id, billed_entity) for a 24-hour window (attached: usage-sample-logs.csv)
- Open a HubSpot ticket and flag as payment-hold priority so our billing team temporarily removes the invoice from collections until we reconcile
- Propose a provisional, reversible credit for any amount we confirm was mis-attributed pending your tax team's validation

Can you confirm which 24-hour window you'd like sampled? If you want the full monthly sampling we'll need ~24 hours to assemble an export. If you prefer a short high-volume window (e.g., Aug 10 00:00–23:59 UTC), we can send that within the hour.

I'll loop in Grace (billing ops) and Marissa (account lead) so we coordinate the provisional credit and legal sign-off.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference
Attachment: usage-sample-logs.csv (text/csv)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 12:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Invoice hold: Aug charges and tax nexus question

Vivek — adding the ops perspective. If Alejandra confirms the window, billing can produce a per-prefix and per-model export that includes: request_id, timestamp, billed_entity_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, and route. That should be sufficient for tax to confirm nexus and whether VAT applies.

If we see misattribution we typically do: (1) issue a provisional credit against the invoice equal to the mis-attributed line items, (2) hold collections while tax validates, and (3) propose a one-time adjustment in the next billing cycle. For UK/EU VAT we also need to know: which Atlas legal entity is registered for VAT, and whether you want us to reclassify the billed_entity retroactively (we can do that but prefer a documented audit trail).

I'll prepare the export after Alejandra confirms the 24-hour sample window. Also adding a notes link to the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890123 (I created ticket HUB-5312).

Grace
Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alejandra Ruiz <alejandra.ruiz@atlasretail.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 26 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Invoice hold: Aug charges and tax nexus question

Alejandra — quick update and proposed path to resolution.

1) You asked for a short sample: we pulled Aug 10 00:00–23:59 UTC as a representative high-volume day and attached the export (usage-sample-logs.csv). The export includes the billed_entity_id column and the per-request routing. We see ~21.8% of token charges from that day attributed to entity 'AT-UK-01' while your supplied tax memo indicates the UK entity should only handle EMEA retail transactions (not global ingestion).

2) Provisional credit: to avoid collection action while your tax/legal team reviews, Redwood has issued a provisional credit of EUR 9,120.00 against INV-20250801. Please find the provisional credit note attached (provisional-credit-note-ATL-0142.pdf). This credit is reversible if our audit shows correct attribution, but we will not send the invoice to collections for 14 days.

3) Evidence we still need from Atlas for retro reclassification: a short statement confirming which legal entity each API key/tenant should be assigned to, and any PO/contract references if the split is tied to customer billing rules. If you prefer, we can accept that as a signed DocuSign; otherwise an email from your finance lead is fine.

4) Next steps timeline: Grace will run the full-month export (24–36 hours) and provide a reconciliation. Until then, please keep the invoice on hold and upload the entity mapping to: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/shared/ATL-0142/usage-samples.

If you want a call to walk through the CSV we can schedule a 30-minute window today.

Best regards,
Vivek
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference
Attachments: usage-sample-logs.csv (text/csv); provisional-credit-note-ATL-0142.pdf (application/pdf)
